prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: hospital medication dispensing/returns; pharmacist oversight, authorization, traceability. Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Morrowglass validates/timestamps authorized clinical-system orders, flags discrepancies, routes review, communicates current status; produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Unresolved/canceled/duplicated/superseded requests are held, not prepared/loaded. Clinical Pharmacist reviews appropriateness/dose/allergies/interactions, temperature/timing suitability, clinical/labeling exceptions; documents disposition before proceeding/authorizing release; produces Dose Exception Review Slip. Copperfield clarifies/escalates, checks contents/patient/order identifiers, packaging/lot/expiry/cold-chain limits; produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Cinderwake prepares authorized orders, records handling, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag; presents packages to Juniper. Release requires order/medication/destination checks against approved instructions. Juniper records outcomes, blocks incomplete-check release, produces Batch Release Note; decisions associate order/package identifiers, verification time, staff credentials. Before delivery-network entry, supporting records establish release/conditions; load manifest identifies packages/destinations/handling/assembly time; identifier comparison detects omissions/substitutions/duplicates. Bluejay continuously records timestamped temperatures, reports excursions/connectivity loss; affected stock segregated pending authorized disposition. Temperature-sensitive packages stay controlled until custody transfer. Hospital Courier transports authorized medication/returns; checks count/integrity/destination/handling, records acceptance time/identity, verifies secure/unexposed capsule closure; produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record. Pneumatic Tube Network accepts packaging/routing-compliant loads. East Tube Dispatch Console checks availability, records route/timing/status, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket for route/deadline failure; West Tube Dispatch Console controls authorized routing. Dispatch holds capsules/blocks faults; Copperfield rechecks retries. Operations coordinates alternatives; faulted segments require safe testing/authorization. Charge Nurse sends Cabinet Downtime Notice, coordinates contingencies/notifications. North Ward Cabinet Controller/South Ward Cabinet Controller block Out of Service dispensing until Ready for Dispense plus checks; Operations closes interruptions after workflow confirmation. Larkspur confirms need/contingencies; ward access remains authorized/accountable. Stonewake repairs/verifies; IT Operations Specialist checks connectivity/interfaces/logs/applications; service

Document units:
S095: Before a capsule is admitted, its package identifiers and destination are reconciled with the prepared load information.
S096: A route or packaging problem places the load on hold until staff resolve the condition and document the outcome.
S097: If automated transfer is unavailable, staff retain custody and use an approved alternate delivery procedure.
S098: The receiving department confirms arrival and reports any discrepancy through the established operational process.
S099: Ward staff perform a receipt check on each arriving load before placing medication in a cabinet or transferring custody.
S100: A Registered Nurse or other authorized ward staff member verifies that the load is intended for the ward.
S101: North Ward Cabinet Controller records the arrival time and the destination cabinet for loads assigned to the north ward.
S102: South Ward Cabinet Controller records the arrival time and the destination cabinet for loads assigned to the south ward.
S103: North Ward Cabinet Controller uses the Priority Refill Tote Tag to confirm the intended ward before staff accept a tote.
S104: Staff inspect the outer packaging for damage, moisture, tampering, or other signs that the load may be unsafe to handle.
S105: Ward staff compare package identifiers with the cabinet task list and confirm that the identifiers are legible.
S106: Cabinet staff verify the quantity and medication descriptions against the expected receipt record.
S107: For refrigerated medication, a Registered Nurse checks that the load remained within the required handling conditions.
S108: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler displays the current temperature and any recorded excursion for staff review.
S109: Staff isolate a load when its identity, quantity, packaging, or temperature condition does not match the expected receipt.
S110: Staff do not place an unresolved load into active cabinet stock.
S111: Accepted medication is staged in the designated receiving area until cabinet placement is authorized.
S112: The ward records receipt completion and any discrepancy through the established operational process.
S113: Ward staff check return bins before use to confirm that each bin is intact, clean, and assigned to the correct return stream.
S114: A Registered Nurse confirms that the contents are eligible for return and are separated from waste and non-medication items.
S115: Staff check that each return bin closes securely and that its contents do not obstruct the closure.
S116: Tallowmere guides ward staff through return-bin checks and records each check outcome for follow-up.
S117: The Pharmacy Technician uses the audit label to identify a return bin for the scheduled collection.
